title: Polynomial-size circuits for EXP
formal: Is \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\)? More explicitly, does there exist a language \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{*}\), decidable by one deterministic exponential-time algorithm, whose circuit complexity \(s_L(n)\) satisfies \[\forall C\geq1\;\forall k\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}\;\forall N\geq1\;\exists n\geq N:\quad s_L(n)>C(n+1)^{k}?\]
why: This is a central test of whether explicit computation can be proved to require large unrestricted Boolean circuits. Resolving it would cross the gap between uniform time hierarchy theorems and lower bounds that defeat arbitrary nonuniform circuit families.
status_note: Conjecture 8.6 is open in the saved 2019 source. On 13 September 2026 the targeted later-work check found a 2026 consistency result, whose abstract does not claim the separation. No full resolution was verified; the later proof was not independently checked. Status remains source_open.

progress.text: The saved book draft states EXP outside P/poly as Conjecture 8.6 and explains its relationship to generating hard truth tables.

The preprint reports that the bounded-arithmetic theory \(S^1_2\) is consistent with the circuit separation. This is a result about formal provability and consistency, not a resolution of the class comparison.

importance.reason: Tests the power of polynomial-size nonuniform computation against exponential-time computation, a central circuit lower-bound question.

sentences: EXP contains problems solvable in deterministic exponential time.
The question asks whether every such problem could nevertheless have polynomial-size Boolean circuits chosen separately for each input length.
The circuits need not be efficiently constructible, making this different from a polynomial-time simulation.
Time hierarchy theorems alone do not eliminate that nonuniform possibility.
The project seeks a lower bound strong enough to defeat arbitrary length-specific circuit designs for some language with an explicit exponential-time decision procedure.

definitions: \(\mathrm{EXP}=\bigcup_{a\geq1}\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{n^{a}})\), with the usual multiplicative constants and polynomially equivalent deterministic multitape Turing-machine encodings. The input is an arbitrary binary string and the machine decides membership without a promise, advice or oracle. A Boolean circuit on \(n\) inputs is an acyclic graph using fan-in-two AND and OR gates, fan-in-one NOT gates, constants, and one output. Its size is the number of noninput gates; replacing this by its explicit gate-and-wire encoding length preserves polynomial size. The quantity \(s_L(n)\) is the minimum such size for exact agreement with membership in \(L\) on all \(n\)-bit strings. Circuit choices for different lengths are arbitrary and need not be computable. The class \(\mathrm{P/poly}\) comprises languages with \(s_L(n)\leq C(n+1)^k\) for all \(n\), for some constants \(C,k\) depending on the language. The quantifiers in the question require one language defeating every polynomial size bound; they do not require a lower bound at every sufficiently large length. The source uses exponential-time notation in a truth-table generation discussion; the card uses the standard union defining EXP. Using \(\mathrm E=\mathrm{DTIME}(2^{O(n)})\) instead gives the equivalent class-containment question by polynomial padding.

context_blocks.text: The deterministic time hierarchy separates polynomial from exponential uniform running time. It does not rule out small circuits chosen independently at each input length, which is the nonuniform issue in this conjecture.

Wigderson states the separation as Conjecture 8.6 in a discussion of explicit hard Boolean functions and pseudorandomness. Counting shows that many truth tables need large circuits, but the conjecture additionally places a hard language in a fixed uniform exponential-time class.

A 2026 preprint by Atserias and Müller proves a consistency result relating bounded arithmetic to \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\). Consistency of the separation with a formal theory is distinct from a proof of the separation itself.

The public note proposes a weaker upper-bound question: whether every EXP language has subexponential-size circuits. For example, one precise convention is \(\forall L\in\mathrm{EXP}\;\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists N\;\forall n\ge N:\ s_L(n)\le 2^{\varepsilon n}\). Polynomial-size circuits would imply this upper bound. It is consequently weaker than the containment \(\mathrm{EXP}\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\), which is the negative answer to the present separation question, rather than a weaker form of the conjectured lower bound. The displayed convention specifies this contextual variant; it is not substituted for the card’s original target.

answer_criterion: Provide a complete Lean-checked proof of \(\mathrm{EXP}\not\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\), including an EXP language and the quantified superpolynomial lower bound, or prove its negation \(\mathrm{EXP}\subseteq\mathrm{P/poly}\). Different hard languages for different fixed exponents, a lower bound for a restricted gate basis, or a consistency theorem alone do not settle the question.
